newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Consob to keep role after EMU start -head-.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Consob to keep role after EMU start -head-.

text.p: Italy's stock market regulator Consob will be subject to changes with the start of the single European currency but will not have to give up its supervisory role to a supernational body, Consob's chairman said.

Tommaso Padoa Schioppa was speaking at a forum on "The euro and globalisation of financial markets: prospects for Italy" as part of the Global 24 international conference on the impact of European monetary union.
"Consob will have to face up to a single European financial market where financial activities will be denominated in a single currency," he said.
"The European central bank will be born, but the controlling and supervisory authorities will remain national linked by a (common) platform represented by European Union directives.

"The national institutions will have to try to make coherent the different sets of rules through voluntary cooperation," Padoa Schioppa said. "I don't think that a supernational institution will be created," he added.
